verdict.rationale: Gazebo's plugin architecture (gz-sim plugins for 'robot, sensor, and environment control', gz-transport messaging, and swappable physics engines via a 'plugin based interface') gives some abstraction that lets an application interact with different simulated sensors/actuators through a common message interface without rewriting core logic. However, this is a simulation-only abstraction (SDF/plugin swapping in sim), not evidence of a stable hardware-abstraction layer for real physical sensors/actuators during hardware bring-up. missing for 10: evidence of real hardware driver abstraction, examples of swapping actual physical sensor/actuator hardware without app code changes, and documentation tying simulated plugin interfaces to real-world HAL consistency.
